image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a tiger beetle on a textured, light-colored ground (likely sand or concrete). The beetle has a dark, metallic body with distinct pale yellow/white spots on its elytra. It features long, slender legs and very long, thin antennae. The head is visible with large eyes.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, appearing broad relative to the neck/pronotum area, and the large, bulging compound eyes are prominent on the sides of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall body shape is elongated and relatively slender, consistent with the cursorial nature of tiger beetles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bright metallic coloration in green, bronze, or copper tones.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are clear, irregular pale yellow/cream spots on the dark elytra, a key identifying feature of many tiger beetle species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Six slender cursorial legs enabling rapid pursuit.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (head, thorax, abdomen).
